projects.name: Resume Skill Matcher

models.name: Resume
models.description: Extracted fields from one candidate resume.

fields.name: skills
fields.description: List of skills with source quotes

models.name: JobDescription
models.description: Required skills from the job posting.

models.name: ResumeBatch
models.description: Combined input - resumes plus job description.

fields.name: matched
fields.description: True if skill is in job requirements

modules.label: Resume Uploads
modules.note: Many candidate resumes in text format.
modules.inputDescription: Plain-text candidate resumes — one upload per candidate

modules.label: Extract Resume Fields
modules.note: One structured Resume per uploaded Document.
modules.inputDescription: List of Document objects — one resume file each
modules.prompt: Extract name (with quote), years of experience (number), optional email (with quote if present), 1-5 fit score (number), and list of skills (each with quote).

modules.label: Link Quotes
modules.note: Auto · Resume → Resume · links LLM quote strings to source spans.

modules.label: Job Description
modules.note: Single job description text file.
modules.inputDescription: Plain-text job description with required skills

modules.label: Parse Job Requirements
modules.note: Extract required skills from job description.
modules.inputDescription: Job description Document text
modules.prompt: List all required technical skills from this job description. Return as a list in required_skills.

modules.label: Combine Inputs Document
modules.note: Merge parsed resumes (pipeline state) with job description.
modules.inputDescription: Resume list from Extract plus job description from Parse

modules.label: Combine Inputs
modules.note: Merge parsed resumes (pipeline state) with job description.
modules.inputDescription: Resume list from Extract plus job description from Parse

modules.label: Flatten Skill Matches
modules.note: ResumeBatch → list[SkillMatch] for spreadsheet output.
modules.inputDescription: Combined ResumeBatch with resumes and job_desc

fallbackList.typescript: (batch) => batch.resumes.flatMap(resume => resume.skills.map(skill => ({ candidate_name: resume.name[0], skill: skill[0], matched: batch.job_desc.required_skills.includes(skill[0]), years_exp: resume.years_exp, fit_score: resume.fit_score })))

modules.label: Skill Matches Output
modules.note: Final spreadsheet output.
modules.inputDescription: List of SkillMatch objects — one row per skill mention

projects.documentation:
# Resume Skill Matcher

1. Upload many candidate resumes (text files)
2. Upload one job description
3. Pipeline extracts resume fields with source quotes
4. Parses required skills from job description
5. Combines inputs and checks skill matches
6. Outputs spreadsheet with one row per skill mention

Fields:
- Quoted: name, email, skills
- Numbers: years_exp, fit_score
- Boolean: matched (skill in requirements)

chat.content: please create a project to summarise a list of documents in a single paragraph.
I'll create a document summarizer pipeline that takes text documents and produces concise one-paragraph summaries. The pipeline will have 3 steps: input → LLM summarization → output.

Build a pipeline for accounts payable: users upload many PDF receipts at once (hundreds). For each receipt extract merchant, date, amount, currency, category, and tax. Every extracted field that comes from the document should be quote-linked back to the source. Output one spreadsheet of all receipt rows. Rename the project to Receipt Spreadsheet.
Pipeline: PDF batch upload → per-receipt field extraction → spreadsheet output. All fields include source quotes.

Fix the receipt spreadsheet so amount and tax are numbers I can sum, not quoted text. Category is a guess (meals, travel) — don't quote it. Currency is often missing, so make it optional plain text. Don't put the original file on each row; that's already the upload. I already uploaded sample_receipt_1.txt and sample_receipt_2.txt — make sure I can actually run with those files.
Updated receipt pipeline: numeric amounts, optional currency, plain category, and removed file reference. Ready to test with your uploaded receipts.

I still cannot run with sample_receipt_1.txt and sample_receipt_2.txt — Inference says the slot wants PDFs. Switch the upload slot to plain text so those files work. Also the extract prompt still tells the model to quote amount and tax, but those fields are numbers now — stop asking for quotes on numeric fields. Keep the existing steps; this is a small fix, not a rebuild.
Fixed: input accepts text files now, and extract prompt only quotes merchant/date. Amount/tax are plain numbers, currency optional.

Build a finance pipeline for our team. We upload many vendor invoices (PDF or photos) each week plus one company travel policy. Extract vendor, invoice date, total, currency, and each line item with quotes back to the invoice text. Flag any line that looks like it violates the travel policy. Output a spreadsheet of all lines with pass/fail plus a short reason. Include a couple of sample invoices and a sample policy so we can try it immediately.
Fixed pipeline: invoice batch → policy → combine → compliance check → output. Added sample invoices and policy for testing.

Build a recruiting screen pipeline.
- Users upload many candidate resumes (plain text files) plus one job description.
- For each resume extract: candidate name (quoted from the resume), years of experience (a number), email (quoted if present, otherwise optional), a 1–5 fit score (inferred, not quoted), and each listed skill as quoted text.
- Then check which skills match the job description.
- Output a spreadsheet of one row per skill mention: candidate name, skill, matched true/false, years of experience, fit score.
- Include 2 sample resumes and 1 job description so we can run immediately. Use text files, not PDFs. Do not emit Convert to text, Parse to structure, or Link Quotes yourself.
Pipeline: batch resume upload → extract fields → parse job → combine → flatten matches → spreadsheet output. Includes sample resumes and job description for testing.
